New paper advised by Li Fei-Fei!

"Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization"

Image generation commonly uses pretrained encoders like DINO as tokenizers, but these can discard visual details important for generation.

So this paper trains encoders to preserve information shared between masked image views, using a generative model to guide learning.

On ImageNet, it improves FID from 2.36 to 2.18 at similar total training compute, with scaling-law extrapolations suggesting 7–8x less tokenizer training compute than DINOv2 and WebSSL.

x.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

tweets.text:
It’s incredible to have reached a threshold where it’s practical that AI will be better at training models than humans are so quickly. One day recursive self improvement feels far off, and the next we already have signs of what it will look like.

Model capability finally exceeding most human engineers, advancements in the harness and infra for long running agents, a growing array of data, and the ability to parallelize the agents to work on vastly more tasks and tests and approaches than any person could have before, creates an incredible flywheel. 

This flywheel will almost certainly accelerate model progress far faster than we’ve seen before - or at a minimum enable pushing up the ceiling of the frontier at an insane rate. If you aren’t pricing in what RSI will lead to, that’s probably a mistake.

So in fact we actually can get robots, flying cars, superintelligence, fast internet on planes, space travel, space colonies, orbital data centers, unlimited energy, likely cures for nearly every disease, and more all in our life times. Pretty great. https://t.co/jhgqv8gXhb

feelings

holding hands, running
through the yellow light

hearing my heart break

midnight to sunrise

When we introduced VM Sandboxes, we wanted to preserve Modal’s sub-second cold starts without compromising performance. 

We ended up building a new filesystem stack that dramatically improved performance, and wrote about the engineering challenges and decisions that got us there.
Learn more and deploy Reflection Beam as a Dedicated Endpoint on Modal: https://t.co/idMbhOfjeQ

Reflection Beam is now available on Modal.

Beam is a 501B-parameter open-weight MoE (23B active) from @reflection_ai built for coding, agentic workflows, and reasoning. It supports a 1M token context window, with token efficiency a core focus.

In early access, the Oura Health Intelligence team found that "Beam had fewer context leaks and was much more grounded in its answers than other frontier models we evaluated.”
